author_prompt:
Author 8 DIFFERENT natural ecommerce customer-service dialogue families in en.
Batch 12; ensure at least four current turns classified as general across this batch.
Each family has its OWN coherent history of 2, 4 or 6 short alternating user/assistant
messages, followed by 3 ALTERNATIVE current user turns, not three sequential turns.
Those alternatives differ in effective intent: retain vs replace, withdraw vs
continue, single goal vs concurrent goal, or resolved vs unresolved reference.
Include natural short answers where history matters. Vary old completed tasks,
hesitation, self-correction, indirect wording, topics and dialogue acts. General
and human-service requests must also occur as NEW goals, not only stale history.
Do not follow a repeated sentence template or substitute product nouns to create
new families. Avoid stereotyped 'information only, do not submit' repetition.
Invent broad everyday ecommerce situations; no copied benchmark or private data.
History plus current turn should fit 150 English words or 180 Chinese characters;
keep it compact but meaningful. No future replies or final conversation summaries.
Supply the correct label for each alternative according to the rubric.

families.scenario: Customer asks about a smartwatch they bought and then shifts to a casual question.

messages.content: Hi, I got the FitPulse S2 watch yesterday. The heart-rate monitor seems off when I run.
Sorry to hear that. Have you tried tightening the strap one notch? Loose contact often causes erratic readings during exercise.
I'll try that. Actually, before I go — do you folks have a physical store downtown?

variants.text: Thanks, I'll test it on my next run and let you know if it still misbehaves.
variants.label: product_technical

variants.text: Wait, forget the watch issue. Is your downtown store open on Sundays?
variants.label: general

variants.text: The strap trick helped, but now the battery drains in six hours. What else can I check?
variants.label: product_technical

families.scenario: Customer asks about a return and then makes small talk.

messages.content: I need to return the desk lamp I ordered last week. The box says model GL-40 but I received GL-30.
That's a mismatch on our end. I can set up a prepaid return label for you. Would you like a replacement or a refund?
Refund is fine. Also, is it supposed to rain here tomorrow? I'm planning a picnic.

variants.text: Refund, please. And yes, I know you're not a weather service — I was just chatting. Thanks for the help.
variants.label: billing_refund

variants.text: Actually, hold the refund. Can you just send me the correct GL-40 instead?
variants.label: billing_refund

variants.text: Never mind the lamp entirely. I'm moving abroad next month — do you ship internationally?
variants.label: order_logistics

families.scenario: Customer asks about order status then asks for a person.

messages.content: My order #48291 was supposed to arrive Tuesday but tracking hasn't updated since Friday.
Let me check that. I see the parcel is with the courier but there was a weather delay in the Midwest hub. It should move again within 24 hours.
Okay. Can you actually connect me to a real person? I've been bounced around all morning.

variants.text: Fine, I'll wait another day. But if it's not here by Thursday I'm filing a complaint.
variants.label: order_logistics

variants.text: Yes, please transfer me to a human agent now.
variants.label: human_service

variants.text: Actually, forget the order — I just realized my account shows a charge I never made. Who handles that?
variants.label: account_security

families.scenario: Customer asks about a coffee maker and then a general question.

messages.content: The BrewMaster 3000 I bought keeps stopping mid-cycle with an E2 error.
E2 usually means the water reservoir isn't seated properly. Could you remove it and push it back in until you hear a click?
That fixed it, thanks! By the way, how long has your company been around?

variants.text: It worked — coffee's brewing now. Appreciate the quick fix.
variants.label: product_technical

variants.text: Just curious about your company history, no other issue. Thanks!
variants.label: general

variants.text: It worked, but now the machine makes a grinding noise on the second cycle. Is that normal?
variants.label: product_technical

families.scenario: Customer asks about a refund and then about a different order.

messages.content: I returned the hiking boots on Monday. When will the refund hit my card?
The return was scanned at our warehouse today. Refunds typically process within 3–5 business days after that scan.
Got it. And can you also check why my tent order from last month shows as delivered but I never got it?

variants.text: Okay, I'll watch for the refund. For the tent, it says delivered to my old address — I moved. Can you help?
variants.label: order_logistics

variants.text: Actually, cancel the refund question — I found the boots in my car, I never mailed them. Sorry!
variants.label: billing_refund

variants.text: Both issues matter to me. First the refund timing, then the missing tent. Let's start with the tent.
variants.label: order_logistics

families.scenario: Customer asks about account lockout then makes a general comment.

messages.content: I can't log in — it says my password is wrong but I'm sure it's correct.
Let's reset it. I'll send a verification code to your registered email. Can you confirm the last four digits of the phone on file?
It's 2291. Also, your website redesign looks really clean, whoever did that.

variants.text: 2291. And yes, the new site is nice — but I still need to get into my account.
variants.label: account_security

variants.text: Actually, I just remembered I have a second account with a different email. Can you help me access that one instead?
variants.label: account_security

variants.text: Never mind the login — I'll deal with it later. Just wanted to say the site looks great. Have a good day!
variants.label: general

families.scenario: Customer asks about a blender replacement part then asks for human help.

messages.content: The pitcher for my BlendPro 500 cracked. Do you sell replacement pitchers separately?
We do — the replacement pitcher for the BlendPro 500 is item #BP500-P, priced at $24.99. It's in stock.
Great. Can I speak to someone about a warranty claim instead? The crack might be a defect.

variants.text: Perfect, I'll order the pitcher. Thanks for the quick answer.
variants.label: product_technical

variants.text: Please connect me to the warranty department — I want a human to review photos of the crack.
variants.label: human_service

variants.text: Actually, is the pitcher covered under the two-year warranty, or do I need to buy it?
variants.label: billing_refund

families.scenario: Customer asks about delivery address change then makes a general remark.

messages.content: I need to change the delivery address for order #77120. It's going to my office but I'll be home next week.
I can update that. What's the new address, and should I also update the shipping method to match the new timeline?
It's 14 Maple Street, unit 3B. And honestly, your chat support is way faster than calling.

variants.text: 14 Maple Street, unit 3B. Standard shipping is fine, thanks.
variants.label: order_logistics

variants.text: Actually, never mind — I'll just have a coworker grab it from the office. No change needed.
variants.label: order_logistics

variants.text: 14 Maple Street, unit 3B. Also, do you price-match if I find the same item cheaper elsewhere?
variants.label: billing_refund
